location_name: Malaysian map of territorial waters and continental shelf boundaries (21 December 1979); Sipadan and Ligitan
summary: Indonesia protested Malaysia's 21 December 1979 map of its territorial waters and continental shelf boundaries (the 'Peta Baru') by a note verbale of 8 February 1980 to the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta, rejecting Malaysia's claimed boundary lines and its claim to Sipadan and Ligitan; Malaysia's Foreign Ministry confirmed in Parliament in June 1980 that Indonesia's protest concerned the new map.
reasoning: A formal protest note rejecting another claimant's published boundary map is a verbal assertion; declarative. The note's best-documented target is Sipadan and Ligitan in the Celebes Sea, outside the South China Sea; whether it also objected to the map's South China Sea shelf lines near Natuna is not stated in the sources opened, so a coder may treat it as out of area. The day comes from Indonesia's ICJ memorial (a PDF that blocks scripted fetching, read through a summarising fetch); the Hansard reply gives no date; the IBRU briefing returned 404 to scripted fetching and was also read through a summarising fetch, so the second and third excerpts are unverified.

location_name: Exclusive Economic Zone of Indonesia (incl. the waters north of the Natuna Islands)
summary: President Soeharto signed and promulgated Law No. 5 of 1983 on the Indonesian Exclusive Economic Zone, giving statutory force to the 1980 declaration: a 200-nautical-mile zone measured from Indonesia's territorial-sea baselines, sovereign rights over its resources, delimitation by agreement where it overlaps neighbours' zones (with the median line applying until then), and criminal penalties of up to Rp 225 million for violations.

reasoning: Legislation establishing and penalising violations of a 200-mile zone that includes waters claimed by Vietnam and within China's dashed line is a legal assertion; declarative. Primary text (Kemenkeu JDIH) and UN DOALOS listing both give 18 October 1983.

summary: Indonesia enacted Law No. 17 of 1985 ratifying the 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea on 31 December 1985, stating that the archipelagic-state regime consolidated Indonesia's position as an archipelagic state under the Wawasan Nusantara and that waters formerly high seas had become Indonesian archipelagic waters; Indonesia deposited its ratification with the UN on 3 February 1986.
actors: President Soeharto; Dewan Perwakilan Rakyat (DPR); Department of Foreign Affairs
reasoning: The ratifying law presents the Convention as international recognition of Indonesia's archipelagic baselines and enclosed waters, including the Natuna group; as a legal assertion of the archipelagic claim it is declarative. Ratifying a multilateral treaty can also be read as cooperative, so a coder may drop it.
